chunks: He said: Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Usamah al-Basri informed me by authorization. He said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Wasiti narrated to us. He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us. He said: Harun ibn Muslim ibn Sa'dan narrated to us. He said: Mas'adah ibn Sadaqah narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from his father, peace be upon them both. Indeed he said:

The Najashi, king of Abyssinia, sent for Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and his companions. They entered upon him while he was in a house of his, sitting on the ground wearing worn-out garments. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said: We were alarmed by his state when we saw him in that condition. When he saw what was with us and the change in our faces, he said:

Praise be to Allah who gave victory to Muhammad, delighted his eye, and strengthened his support. Shall I not give you glad tidings? I said: Yes, O King. He said: A spy of mine from the land of your people has just come to me and informed me that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave victory to His Prophet Muhammad, and destroyed his enemy. Such and such persons were captured, and such and such persons were killed. They met at a place called Badr - as if I am looking at it, for I used to tend sheep there for my master from the Banu Damrah.

Ja'far said: So I said to him: What is wrong with you that you sit on the ground and wear these worn-out garments? He said: We find in what was revealed to Jesus son of Mary that among the rights of Allah upon His servants is that they show humility when Allah bestows a new blessing upon them. And since Allah has bestowed upon me the blessing of Muhammad, I have shown this humility.

When the Prophet was informed of this, he said to his companions: Charity increases a person's wealth, so give charity and Allah will have mercy on you. And humility elevates a person's rank, so be humble and Allah will elevate you. And forgiveness increases a person's honor, so forgive and Allah will honor you.

key_terms.الإِجَازَة: Authorization to transmit a text or teaching through a chain of scholars
key_terms.النَّجَاشِيّ: The Negus, the Christian king of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) who sheltered the early Muslim migrants
key_terms.بَدْر: Location of the first major battle in Islamic history (624 CE) where Muslims decisively defeated the Quraysh
key_terms.بَنُو ضَمْرَة: An Arab tribe near Badr; the Najashi reveals he was once a slave who tended sheep there

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad teach about charity, humility, and forgiveness when he heard of the Najashi's humble response to the victory at Badr?
ai.summary: This narrative recounts how the Najashi of Abyssinia demonstrated profound humility upon learning of the Muslim victory at Badr. Despite being a powerful king, he sat on the bare ground in worn garments to thank God for the blessing of Muhammad's triumph. When asked about his humble appearance, the Najashi cited a teaching revealed to Jesus that God's servants should show humility when receiving new blessings. The Prophet Muhammad, upon hearing of the Najashi's humility, taught his companions three interconnected virtues: charity increases wealth, humility elevates rank, and forgiveness increases honor.
